Items.Authors: Ricardo Zanmar Sanchez, Salvatore Savarese, Vittorio Braga, Marcella Di Criscienzo, Giuliana Fiorentino, Pietro Schipani, Laura Schreiber, Joshua Meyers, Sandrine J. Thomas
Items.Title: A wavefront sensing method based on science image analysis: application to the Vera C. Rubin Observatory
Items.Abstract: We present a wavefront sensing technique based on the analysis of elongation patterns of science star fields. Our method relies on a parametric model to calculate the wavefront error throughout the focal plane and we use it to analytically derive moments of stars. With numerical optimization we find the corresponding misalignments (rigid body and mirror deformations) that best reproduce a given ellipticity pattern of stars. In this work we apply the method to science images observed during the commissioning of the LSST of the Vera C. Rubin observatory and present some lessons learned and limitations of this technique.

Items.Authors: Nicolas Doucet, Damien Gratadour, Cyril Tasse
Items.Title: Accelerating facet-based gridding and degridding with GPUs
Items.Abstract: The SKA radio telescope project requires efficient processing of massive data volumes  We developed a GPU accelerated Baseline Dependent Averaging gridder capable of handling Direction Dependent Effects, including Jones matrices. That implementation is integrated into DDFacet for full pipeline testing and comparison.

Items.Authors: Daniel Lancaster, Stefan Kraus, Sorabh Chhabra, Owain Snaith, Jyotirmay Paul
Items.Title: Acceptance testing of the CRED ONE camera for BIFROST
Items.Abstract: BIFROST is soon to be part of the ASGARD visitor suite of instruments for the Very Large Telescope Interferometer (VLTI). BIFROST will have two spectrographs that can be used together for fringe tracking and for different spectral resolutions. Both spectrographs will be equipped with their own First Light Imaging CRED ONE NIR camera. The design and implementation of these two cameras is different to that of a normal CRED ONE. The camera is designed for ultra-low noise and a slower acquisition rate. To achieve this, the cold-stop aperture of the system is minimised to still accept the beam of BIFROST but minimise background light. In this paper we will discuss the acceptance testing preformed in December 2024 and follow up testing later in the year. This will include acceptance F-number characterisation as well as sensor performance metrics.

Items.Authors: Michael J. Ireland, Frantz Martinache, Stefan Kraus, Denis Defrère, Peter Tuthill, Daniel Ahrer, Fatmé Allouche, Emilie Bouzerand, Julia Bryant, Joshua Carter, Sorabh Chhabra, Benjamin Courtney-Barrer, Fred Crous, Nick Cvetojevic, Daniel Dahl, Steve Ertel, Juan Pablo Gil, Adrian Glauser, Xavier Habois, Lucas Labadie, Stéphane Lagarde, Daniel Lancaster, Connor Langford, Romain Laugier, Roxanne Ligi, Grace McGinness, Marc-Antoine Martinod, Alexandra Mazzoli, Anthony Meilland, Kwinten Missiaen, Sébastien Morel, Barnaby Norris, Laurent Pallanca, Jyotirmay Paul, Romain Petrov, Nicholas Schuhler, Gert Raskin, Sylvie Robbe-Dubois, J. Gordon Robertson, Ahmed Sanny, Owain Snaith, Adam Taras
Items.Title: Achieving the highest angular resolution and contrast with Asgard instrumental suite for ESO’s VLTI: commissioning results and projected performance
Items.Abstract: Asgard is a suite of visitor instrument modules for the ESO’s Very Large Telescope Interferometer designed to deliver high-contrast interferometric capability at infrared wavelengths through the phased installation of adaptive-optics, fringe-tracking, spectroscopic, and nulling instrumentation. The full instrumental suite will deliver by far the highest spectral and spatial resolution in the southern hemisphere (1 milli-arcsec and R~25,000 in Y with BIFROST), while also enabling exoplanet characterisation at 4-milli-arcsec resolution and 105 contrast in the L’ band using Nott. The first phase (Heimdallr, Baldr and Solarstein) is commissioned, the second phase underway, and the third phase due for completion early 2027. We will report on design, commissioning performance and anticipated scientific reach of the full instrument suite.

Items.Authors: Jocelyn Ferrara
Items.Title: Adaptive beyond optics: scalable project assurance for diverse astronomical instrumentation programs
Items.Abstract: Programs at Caltech Optical Observatories span a wide range of technical complexity, stakeholder expectations, and budgets, making one-size-fits-all project assurance impractical for 5–30 m telescope instruments. With a single Systems Engineer responsible for end-to-end assurance, a scalable, efficient strategy was needed. We developed an adaptive framework that tailors industry and NASA standards, providing scalable plans for requirements, risk/hazard control, configuration management, QA, and EH&S. Accessible tools and templates enable all team members to integrate assurance into daily workflows. Implementation has improved requirements stability, documentation quality, and early identification of integration and safety hazards. This paper describes the framework, deployment lessons, and guidance for observatories seeking effective assurance under constrained resources.

Items.Authors: Andreas Sinn, Georg Schitter
Items.Title: Adaptive optics for small telescope systems in space debris observation and free-space optical communication
Items.Abstract: Small telescope systems are powerful tools for observation of space debris objects, as well as active satellites in low-Earth-orbit (LEO). Free-space optical (FSO) communication provides high-speed data transmission for downlink and global communication. The influence of atmospheric turbulence, vibrations and wind shake limits the achievable performance. An adaptive optics system addressing the requirements of both applications is implemented and evaluated on a horizontal link under severe turbulence. An improvement of the RMS wavefront error by a factor of 4.8 is achieved.

Items.Authors: P. Janin-Potiron, M. Gray, B. Neichel, J.-F. Sauvage, C. T. Heritier, P. Jouve, R. Fetick, A. Carlotti, T. Fusco
Items.Title: Advancements in estimating differential pistons for the Extremely Large Telescope using deep learning II: exploiting defocused images
Items.Abstract: The optical performance of the ELT relies on the precise estimation and correction of differential pistons between the six petals that form the M4 mirror. In a previous study, we demonstrated that a residual network can effectively estimate the differential piston from 2×2 Shack–Hartmann (SH) images, using one trained network per subaperture.  We now extend this approach to a different sensing configuration using defocused images as input, recovering all five differential pistons from a single image. We evaluate the sensitivity of this sensor concept with respect to key variables (number of averaged frames, atmospheric turbulence strength, detector noise).  Furthermore, we exploit multi-wavelength measurements and show that feeding three wavelengths simultaneously to the network enhances the capture range with minimal modifications to the baseline architecture. Finally, we acquired petaled PSF on the HCM bench at IPAG and are now in the process of estimating piston from real images.

Items.Authors: Jill Juneau, Declan O'Neill, Peter Orel, Eric Miller, Sven Herrmann, Gregory Prigozhin, Robert Goeke, Elio Angilè, Mark Bautz, Steven Allen, Tanmoy Chattopadhyay, Kevan Donlon, Michelle Gabutti, Catherine E. Grant, Beverly LaMarr, Christopher Leitz, Glenn Morris, Abigail Y. Pan, Tonya Peshel, Haley Stueber, Keith Warner
Items.Title: Advancing x-ray camera front-end electronics architecture through the AXIS-TAP technology platform
Items.Abstract: The Advanced X-ray Imaging Satellite (AXIS), a NASA Probe-class mission concept, drove the development of a high-speed (≥5 fps) camera Front-End Electronics (FEE) architecture applicable to future soft X-ray missions. To validate the core signal chain (analog-to-digital conversion, FPGA processing, and Ethernet transmission) a technology demonstrator, AXIS-TAP (ADC Testing and Acquisition Platform), has been designed using commercial equivalents of radiation-tolerant components. AXIS-TAP interfaces with the STA Archon benchtop system, enabling simultaneous image acquisition to validate that the flight-like architecture achieves equivalent or superior noise performance. This paper presents the FEE framework, the AXIS-TAP design, and principles enabling scalability to future soft X-ray missions.

Items.Authors: Mingfu Shao, Jiaben Lin, Hui Wang, Liyue Tong, Yuyang Li
Items.Title: An end-to-end pipeline for multimodal solar flare forecasting dataset construction
Items.Abstract: Solar flares are primary drivers of space weather; forecasting eruption from photospheric magnetograms remains a central challenge for solar physics. Existing flare datasets often provide short temporal coverage, single-modality releases, rigid label systems, and risk cross-split leakage when samples from the same active region (AR) appear in both training and test partitions. We present \textbf{JW-FD} (JinWu Flare Dataset), a long-horizon multimodal benchmark built through a documented six-step automated pipeline. JW-FD links NOAA X-ray flare events to 600$\times$600~pixel SDO/HMI line-of-sight magnetogram crops tracked per NOAA AR, spanning 1~January~2011 through 31~December~2024 (14~years). The release comprises 2{,}687 independent ARs, 1{,}750{,}184 co-registered snapshots, and 2{,}687 per-AR evolution videos, exported as FITS, PNG, CSV, and MP4 modalities. Each CSV record binds 29 magnetic features, 35 configurable flare-label fields, and 2 metadata columns (66~dimensions total).

Items.Authors: Rachel A. Cooper, Aarynn Carter, Kevin Volk, Joseph Filippazzo, Tyler Baines, Loïc Albert
Items.Title: An improved correction for 1/f noise in JWST time-series observations
Items.Abstract: We present the development and implementation of a 1/f (flicker) noise correction for time-series observations taken by the NIRISS/SOSS observing mode of the James Webb Space Telescope. The method uses a group-wise scaled median image subtraction to isolate and remove correlated detector noise. We demonstrate that the uncorrected spectra produced by the calibration pipeline exhibited high levels of scatter, and the existing correction provided only modest improvement. We developed a standalone Python implementation compatible with the JWST calibration pipeline and demonstrated significant suppression of flicker noise. After incorporation into the official pipeline and further optimization, the residual RMS of transit light curve fits was reduced by more than 80% in the data tested. This method has been adapted for use with other JWST NIR time-series observing modes, where validation is ongoing.

Items.Authors: Pierre R. Nicolas, Patrick Ingraham, Heejoo Choi, Ewan S. Douglas, Solvay Blomquist, Kevin Derby, Daewook Kim
Items.Title: An open-source Python pipeline for optical performances and alignment analysis using ray-tracing tools
Items.Abstract: This paper presents a fast, accurate, and easily integratable open-source pipeline for analyzing optical system performance under mechanical and thermal perturbations. Built on the Batoid ray-tracing library, the method replaces complex multi-tool workflows with a unified Python-based framework. It processes design variations such as alignment errors, rigid-body motions, and surface deformations-imported directly from standard finite-element-analysis (FEA) outputs-and applies them to the optical model. The pipeline includes automated conversion of Zemax prescriptions, deformation ingestion, system updating, and extraction of optical diagnostics. Using a three-mirror anastigmat telescope and sample Structural-Thermal-Optical-Performance (STOP) data, the paper demonstrates the pipeline's ability to rapidly compute wavefront error, boresight shifts, optical motions, and surface deformation impacts. This approach enables fast feedback loops for design teams and accelerates the development.

Items.Authors: Alexandra N. Higley, Randall McEntaffer, Bridget O'Meara, James Tutt, Jake McCoy, Ross McCurdy, Jeffrey De Lucca, Tristen Sextro, Aditi Gangadharan, Garrett Brady, Cooper Akers, Nathaniel Hamme, Alberto Moretti, Daniele Spiga, Stefano Basso, Vadim Burwitz, Gisela Hartner, Andreas Langmeier, Thomas Müller, Surangkhana Rukdee, Thomas Schmidt, Andrew Holland, Daniel Evan, Karen Holland, David Colebrook, David Gopinath, Max Collon, David Girou, Nicolas Barrière, Marc Verschuuren, Manuel Paans, Jeroen Haneveld, Mark Olde Riekerink, Bart Schurink, Casey DeRoo, Benjamin Donovan, William Zhang, Ryan McClelland, Kai-Wing Chan, Raul Riveros, Michael Biskach, Peter Solly, Timo Saha
Items.Title: An overview of the off-plane grating rocket experiment pathfinder (OGRE-P)
Items.Abstract: The Off-plane Grating Rocket Experiment (OGRE) is a sounding rocket mission that is designed to demonstrate high-performance next-generation X-ray technology for soft X-ray spectroscopy. The nominal payload features a three-component spectrometer consisting of a modern X-ray mirror assembly, modules of blazed reflection gratings with radial groove profiles, and an array of electron-multiplying CCDs. While in flight, OGRE aims to obtain the highest resolution soft X-ray spectrum of Capella to date. As modern X-ray mirror technology continues to develop, the OGRE team will launch a pathfinder mission that uses an existing mirror assembly, JET-X, in preparation for the nominal flight. This preliminary flight, designated as Pathfinder OGRE (OGRE-P), will test the X-ray reflection gratings for high-resolution spectroscopy and provide critical information on the in-flight operation of OGRE payload systems. Here. we report on the current status of the OGRE-P payload.

Items.Authors: Jordan Raffard, Pierre Vermot, Damien Gratadour, Florian Ferreira, Arnaud Sevin
Items.Title: Analysis of deep learning-based methods for denoising pyrWFS adaptive optics for the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT)
Items.Abstract: The Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) has made adaptive optics (AO) essential for ground-based observatories, enabling real-time correction of atmospheric distortions to sharpen astronomical images. Current AO systems rely on pyramid wavefront sensors (pyrWFS), which, despite their high sensitivity, suffer from noise-induced measurement errors—especially when observing faint stars. This degradation limits performance in low-light conditions.  To overcome this, we propose using deep learning to enhance AO control loops by developing neural networks to denoise pyrWFS measurements. We designed several models and integrated them in AO simulations. Evaluations showed significant improvements in Strehl Ratio (SR) and system stability, demonstrating that deep learning can boost AO reliability, even in challenging conditions.  This approach advances AO technology, enabling high-fidelity imaging of faint celestial objects and unlocking the full potential of next-generation telescopes like the ELT.

Items.Authors: Pia Knopp, Alexander Altmann, Norbert Meidinger, Thomas Bechteler, Rafael Strecker, Jonas Mügge, Valeria Antonelli, Vadim Burwitz, Peter Lechner, Robert Andritschke, Max Goretti, David K. Fink, Carlo Fiorini
Items.Title: Analysis of electronic crosstalk effects in a 19-cell silicon drift detector for the eXTP mission
Items.Abstract: The enhanced X-ray Timing and Polarimetry mission (eXTP) aims to explore the state of ultra-dense matter under extreme conditions of gravity and magnetism. A primary instrument of the satellite is the Spectroscopic Focusing Array (SFA) made up of six X-ray focusing telescopes of which five carry a 19-cell Silicon Drift Detector (SDD) each.   The SFA has to meet the crucial requirements of high detector throughput (system deadtime less than 5 % at 1 Crab), high time resolution below 10 μs, and good spectral resolution (energy resolution at 6 keV better than 180 eV). Fast readout of the detector signals is done by three high time resolution spectroscopy (HTRS) ASICs. To improve the spectral resolution, it is important to minimize electronic crosstalk effects in the detector system.   This paper explores the origin of electronic crosstalk in the detector system caused by proximity of signal lines or during signal processing with the goal of optimizing system performance in the future.

Items.Authors: Lawrence S. Jones, Chris A. S. Parmenter, Boris van Griensven, Archie Monk, Matthew Tildesley, Matthew J. Clapp, Nick R. Waltham
Items.Title: Analysis of event detecting front end electronics for x-ray optimised CIS detectors
Items.Abstract: In this work the authors discuss the technical challenges of operating X-ray CMOS image sensors (CIS) with photon counting event detection algorithms incorporated within the front end electronics (FEE). Implementing event detection algorithms early in the signal chain mitigates many of the system design impacts resulting from the high output data rate of these large format (>1 k by 1 k pixels) and high framerate (>10 fps) detectors. However, the FEE is typically resource constrained and therefore incorporating additional computational hardware within this subsystem brings with it significant engineering challenges.  With reference to experimental data, the authors explore the challenges arising from FEE based event detection implementations. This work focusses on the trade-offs that require consideration of detector behaviours to ensure that the scientific performance of the host instrument is maintained whilst still realising the benefits of using CIS detectors in X-ray applications.

Items.Authors: P. Di Marcantonio, H. C. Stempels, V. Alberti, M. Amate, V. Baldini, F. Baron, P. Berio, J. Brynnel, A. Cabral, B. Chazelas, L. Christensen, M. Debus, C. Füßlein, W. Gaessler, O. Gabella, E. Gallo, D. Giannone, R. Gillespie, E. Giro, Y. Ivanisenko, H. Korhonen, I. C. Leão, A. Marconi, P. Masłowski, M. A. Monteiro, E. Pinna, M. Porru, M. Rainer, C. Selmi, F. Sortino, R. Spiga, A. Tozzi, B. Wehbe, A. Zanutta, J. Zimara
Items.Title: ANDES, the high resolution spectrograph for the ELT: insights and lessons from the preliminary design phase
Items.Abstract: The paper introduces the management approach adopted during the Preliminary Design Phase for ANDES, the ESO/ELT high-resolution spectrograph. ANDES’s technical and organizational complexity — stemming from multiple subsystems and a large international consortium - called for a staggered strategy in which the overall preliminary design review was broken down into a series of subsystem-level reviews. We present an in-depth analysis of the lessons learned from implementing this decentralized methodology, examining the advantages and disadvantages encountered and outlining key recommendations to streamline the upcoming project phases.

Items.Authors: Michel Lortholary, Nathan Leguay, Thibault Pichon, Bastien Reboul, Christophe Cara, Gregory Kaszubiak
Items.Title: ARIEL-AIRS electrical ground support equipment (EGSE): building a flexible hardware and software solution that could be used for future projects
Items.Abstract: The ARIEL space telescope (ESA) will study the atmosphere of hundreds of exoplanets through its infrared spectrometer, named AIRS developed by a French consortium of laboratories. To enable this development, CEA teams have worked on a flexible and reliable solution of EGSE.    The EGSE shall allow the full control and readout of the two acquisition chains of the instrument : communication with the AIRS Detector Control Unit (A-DCU), power supply, images and housekeeping data acquisition and their display in real time, data storage and log of all sent commands.    We have build five EGSEs fully integrated into movable racks that can easily follow AIRS on various testing environments.    The software is made of LabVIEW (NI) for the graphic interfaces and Python to build elaborated sequences of tests.  The modularity and parametrization of these EGSEs would enable to adapt the software to next missions which require the same needs.

Items.Authors: Thomas Mattheussen, Denis Defrère, Germain Garreau, Peter Marley Chingaipe, Gert Raskin, Muhammad Salman, Kwinten Missiaen, Bart Vandenbussche, Romain Laugier, Wannes Verstraeten, Johan Morren, Michael J. Ireland, Marc-Antoine Martinod, Ahmed Sanny, Simon Gross, Lucas Labadie, Azzurra Bigioli, András P. Joó, Stephen J. Madden, Alexandra Mazzoli, György Medgyesi, Alen Kuriakose, Steve Ertel, Thomas Stuber, Jeremy Scott, Stefan Kraus, Frantz Martinache, Xavier Haubois, Nicolas Schuhler
Items.Title: Asgard/NOTT: status of laboratory nulling performance
Items.Abstract: Asgard/NOTT will leverage recent VLTI/GRAVITY+ upgrades and integrated optics beam combiners in the mid-infrared to become the first long-baseline nulling interferometer to probe the promising L’ band (3.5-4.0 um). Its aim is to directly image young giants near the snowline of nearby main-sequence stars, combining the VLTI’s 130m-long effective baseline with the high-contrast capability of nulling to reach the required sensitivity. We aim to demonstrate the required nulling sensitivity and stability on the test bench at KU Leuven.     This presentation gives an overview of the current nulling performance, optimization efforts, and limiting factors. Following broadband self-calibrated null depth measurements of (1.14±0.01)×10^-3, we present the first dispersed null depths. The throughput up to the chip is expected to be >40% after optimization and >25% after injection into the chip. We conclude with an outlook on the remaining optimization milestones and the expected on-sky performance.

Items.Authors: Daniel Echeverri, Nemanja Jovanovic, Ashley Baker, Mitsuko Roberts, Yann Terrien, Reston Nash, Tatum Umiamaka, Garreth Ruane, Ricardo Meneses, James Brugger, Cody Lammer, Dimitri Mawet, Robert Bertz
Items.Title: Assembly and characterization of the front-end instrument (FEI) subsystem of Keck/HISPEC
Items.Abstract: The High-Resolution Infrared Spectrometer for Exoplanet Characterization (HISPEC) is a diffraction-limited, single mode fiber-fed, near-infrared spectrograph for the Keck Observatory that will deliver R~100,000 spectra across the y-K bands simultaneously (0.98–2.5 μm). This paper covers the front-end instrument (FEI) subsystem, which injects adaptive-optics-corrected light into the fiber bundles. We present the as-built FEI design and laboratory results validating various elements and end-to-end performance. This includes the tracking system, the dual-bundle injection and PIAA-enabled coupling gains, and an update on the fiber-nulling mode. Finally, we outline the timeline toward FEI delivery to Keck ahead of full-instrument deployment in 2027.

Items.Authors: Daniel P. Violette, Regina Caputo, Adrien Laviron, Kavic Kumar, Zachary Metzler, Grant Sommer, Nicolas Striebig, Richard Leys, Ivan Peric, Manoj Jadhav, Bobae Kim, Jessica Metcalfe, Abhradeep Roy, Yusuke Suda, Yasushi Fukazawa, Norito Nakano
Items.Title: A-STEP: payload integration and launch status
Items.Abstract: A medium-energy (100 keV to 100 MeV) gamma-ray telescope capable of spectroscopy, imaging, and polarization will deepen our understanding of the most energetic astrophysical phenomena and processes. To enable science in this regime, low-power and tileable detector technologies must be developed while still maintaining high spatial and spectral resolution capabilities. AstroPix detectors are high voltage monolithic active pixel sensors (HV-MAPS) that couple the above properties with on-chip signal digitization. The AstroPix Sounding Rocket Technology Demonstration Payload (A-STEP) will be the first operating AstroPix detectors in a space environment and a step towards larger integrated AstroPix systems. A-STEP seeks to detect charged particle tracks in the ionosphere as they pass through a stack of three layered 2x2 AstroPix detector arrays. I will provide highlights from A-STEP’s calibration and integration campaign, along with updates on launch readiness and timeline.

Items.Authors: Peter P. Pedersen, David Degen, Lionel Garcia, Urs Schroffenegger, Daniel Sebastian, Sebastián Zúñiga-Fernández, Brice-Olivier Demory, Elsa Ducrot, Michaël Gillon, Matthew J. Hooton, Clàudia Janó-Muñoz, James McCormac, Mathilde Timmermans, Amaury H. M. J. Triaud, Didier Queloz
Items.Title: Astra: an open-source fully autonomous robotic observatory control software
Items.Abstract: Here we present Astra (Automated Survey observaTory Robotised with Alpaca) OCS, an open-source, cross-platform Python system for the sustained, fully autonomous operation of astronomical observatories, requiring no external message-broker infrastructure. Astra controls observatory hardware via the ASCOM Alpaca protocol, and executes prescheduled observatory actions under continuous safety supervision. Its multi-device actions include plate-solve-based pointing correction with a local Gaia--2MASS catalogue fallback, PID-controlled autoguiding, and autofocus. A FastAPI web service provides a browser UI, REST and WebSocket APIs for real-time status, image previews, and SQLite-backed telemetry and logs.  Astra has run in fully unattended production since January 2024, scaling to six telescopes across three facilities: the four-unit SPECULOOS-South network (Chile), SAINT-EX (Mexico), and the ETH Observatory (Switzerland), with no schedule aborts attributable to Astra software.

Items.Authors: Hervé Geoffray, Beaumont Sophie, Vivian Bernard, Christophe Daniel, Brian Jackson, Simon Bandler, Laurent Ravera, Damien Prêle, Randy Doriese, Mikko Kirivanta, Steve Smith, Edoardo Cucchetti, Peille Philippe
Items.Title: Athena X-IFU detection chain early demonstrations: status and results
Items.Abstract: X-IFU instrument, the high-resolution X-ray spectrometer of the ESA Athena mission, will deliver spectra in the 0.2-12 keV range with a spectral resolution requirement of 4 eV up to 7 keV from 5" pixels, and a field of view of 4'. The detection chain is one of the major functional chains of the X-IFU instrument. CNES leads the project development for the X-IFU Consortium; partners of the main detection chain are NASA-GFSC, SRON, VTT, APC, NIST, IRAP, and IAP. This paper focuses on the results obtained on the detection Demonstrator Models.

Items.Authors: Manuel Gonzalez, Damien Prêle, Si Chen, Jean Mesquida, Alain Givaudan, Michael Punch, Cedric Verilhac, Mael Le Cam, Bernard Courty, Laurent Grandsire
Items.Title: ATHENA X-IFU warm front-end electronics evolution
Items.Abstract: The Warm Front-End Electronics (WFEE) of the X-IFU instrument on ESA’s ATHENA mission provide TES and SQUID biasing, low-noise amplification, and multiplexing signal conditioning. We present recent advances following the development and successful testing of the WFEE Demonstration Model integrating the AwaXe\_v3 ASICs in AMS 350 nm technology. A subsequent prototype generation in an ST node showed good performance but revealed reproducibility issues; this technology remains under investigation for future evolution. To ensure a robust path toward the Engineering Model (EM), a final AMS-based fabrication run has adopted a modular architecture with separate biasing and low-noise amplifier ASICs. We summarize the updated design, lessons learned, and initial results as the WFEE EM development progresses.

Items.Authors: Marina Vela Nuñez, Alessio Pannocchia, Luca Serafini, Pierpaolo Merola, Vladimiro Noce, Elisabetta Giani, Simone Chiarucci, Marianna Michelangnoli, Gianluca Marotta, Mauro Focardi
Items.Title: Automated Verification of the ARIEL Instrument Control Unit Boot Software using Tcl-based Test Sequences
Items.Abstract: The Boot Software (BSW) of space instruments is mission-critical, ensuring safe and reliable transition from power-on to operational state. This paper focuses on the BSW developed for the Instrument Control Unit (ICU) of the ARIEL payload of ESA’s M4 mission. An automated test based on TCL-scripts has been implemented to verify BSW functionalities via TCL test sequences, covering key services such as request verification, housekeeping, event reporting, memory and time management, connection tests, and on-board parameter management. The validation campaign has been executed on the Spacecraft Interface Simulator (SIS) and across multiple instrument models, with the current campaign performed on the ICU Engineering Model (EM). Results show improved repeatability, requirement coverage, early anomaly detection, and reduced manual effort, with methodology reusable for regression campaigns, Full Functional Tests (FFT), and future in-flight verification.

Items.Authors: Florian Quatresooz, Jérôme Henrion, Cyril Petit, Aurélie Montmerle-Bonnefois, Gaël Kermarrec, David Alaluf, Nicolas Védrenne
Items.Title: Automatic exploitation of adaptive optics telemetry for optical turbulence characterization and FSOC performance estimation
Items.Abstract: Characterization of atmospheric turbulence on free-space optical communication (FSOC) links is essential for  optimizing FSOC performance and enabling mitigation approaches such as predictive adaptive optics. To address  this challenge, we recently developed a real-time turbulence monitoring pipeline for FEELINGS, ONERA’s optical  ground station near Toulouse, France. The pipeline provides estimates of integrated turbulence parameters, as  well as Cn2 and wind profiles derived from adaptive optics telemetry. In this work, we present turbulence statistics  collected during GEO-satellite links in fall 2025 and demonstrate how these measurements can be used to assess  FSOC performance metrics.

Items.Authors: Cong Pan, Shihai Yang, Yun Li, Zhuangzhuang Deng, Yanpeng Guo, Jiajia Li, Penxu Fan
Items.Title: Azimuth bandwidth analysis of the 14.5-meter optical-infrared telescope
Items.Abstract: This paper focuses on the design of the azimuth-axis servo control system for a 14.5-meter optical-infrared telescope. A systematic analysis of control bandwidth is conducted, considering both mechanical structural dynamics and wind load disturbances. Based on system parameters and finite element analysis results, a two-mass spring-damping model is established as the core mechanistic representation. Using this model, the influence of mechanical resonance frequency on closed-loop control bandwidth, dynamic performance (overshoot, rise time, settling time), and steady-state error is thoroughly investigated. Results show that, while maintaining comparable dynamic performance, control bandwidth increases significantly with higher mechanical resonance frequencies. Under identical control parameters, increasing the resonance frequency effectively improves dynamic response, reducing overshoot and settling time.

Items.Authors: David Chaparro, Kevin Phan, Enrique De Alba, Zachary Gazak
Items.Title: Background subtraction and dynamic range compression for enhanced satellite detection in telescope imagery
Items.Abstract: Modern space situational awareness systems rely on machine learning for automated resident space object (RSO) tracking. We examine the impact of five background subtraction methods and four dynamic range compression methods on peak RSO F1 detection score. We train a RetinaNet model for 50 epochs over five trials on rate-tracked telescope imagery preprocessed with background subtraction and dynamic range compression, holding all other hyperparameters constant. Our results indicate that Log Inner Quartile Range dynamic range compression raises mean peak F1 by 1.8 percentage points to 0.969, driven by a 3.2\% increase in mean precision over baseline. Background subtraction methods enhance mean peak F1 by ~1\%, driven by a ~2.7\% increase in mean precision. Our work quantifies the impact of background subtraction and dynamic range compression on peak F1 detection score, offering a low-cost, retroactive method to boost RSO detection accuracy without requiring additional data.

Items.Authors: Aravind B. Valluvan, Steven E. Boggs, Andreas Zoglauer, Sophia Haight, Jarred Roberts, Albert Shih, John A. Tomsick
Items.Title: Benchmarking Geant4 activation simulations using proton beam irradiation
Items.Abstract: The Compton Spectrometer and Imager (COSI) is a gamma-ray space telescope launching in 2027 that is designed to survey the entire sky between 0.2 and 5 MeV. A major challenge in analyzing MeV data arises due to the strong, temporally-varying gamma-ray background produced by high-energy particles bombarding the spacecraft. Accurate estimation of the in-flight background spectrum is essential for both scientific analysis and predicting COSI’s observational sensitivity. To validate and refine existing Monte Carlo simulations of the background, we performed multiple controlled proton irradiations on a COSI detector, replicating key aspects of the space radiation environment. Here, we present benchmarking results comparing simulations with experimentally measured data, and demonstrate their impact on predicting COSI’s activation background and overall sensitivity.

Items.Authors: Louis C. Desdoigts, Sebstiaan Haffert, Laird Close, Jared Males, Maggie Kautz, Olivier Guyon
Items.Title: Bridging the gap: high dynamic range piston-mode recovery and non-linear wavefront reconstruction algorithms using the HDFS
Items.Abstract: Segmented ELT pupils introduce large differential piston modes that standard wavefront sensors cannot track. The Holographic Dispersed Fringe Sensor (HDFS) addresses this by converting segment pairs into spectrally dispersed interferometers with multi-wave capture range. We present efficient linear piston-recovery algorithms operating in the Fourier domain, where the differential piston signal becomes linear and resilient to residual aberrations. We then extend the approach using a differentiable forward model of the HDFS to perform non-linear wavefront reconstruction, recovering low-order modes not well suited for purely inverse methods. Together these methods establish a unified, high-dynamic-range reconstruction framework suitable for ELT phasing and future telemetry-driven wavefront control architectures.

Items.Authors: Hugo Rousset, Manon Lizzana, Sébastien Soler, Fabrice Pancher, Julien Michelot, Logi Olgeirsson, Jean Baptiste Le Bouquin, Fabien Malbet
Items.Title: Calibration of pixel grid location of a CMOS silicon matrix detector based on Young’s fringes for space-based high accuracy astrometry
Items.Abstract: In the context of exoplanet detection an hosted payload on the future NASA's HWO has been proposed. The purpose of this proposal is to detect Earth-like planets at distances of up to 10 parsecs using the star's astrometric signal. In order to detect this signal, the centroid of the star must be measured at sub-microarcsecond precision. The preliminary error budget necessitates a pixel position knowledge requirement on the focal plane geometry of down to 5e-5pix. Researchers have been working on a calibration method based on the projection of scrolling Young's fringes on a matricial detector. This method is used to measure the geometrical shift of the pixel's peak response. The present study involves the simulation of the aforementioned calibration method and sensitivities to instrumentation instabilities. Subsequently, the positional coordinates of the initial pixel were determined through the utilisation of a dedicated testbed that was derived from the work of (Crouzier, 2016).

Items.Authors: Dominique Heinis, Joan Torras Estruch, Alejandro Sánchez, Antonio Carballedo, Giuseppe Vacanti, David Girou, Marcos Bavdaz, Albert Van Eeckhout
Items.Title: Calibration of the Minerva beamline for the characterization of the mirror modules of the NewAthena space telescope
Items.Abstract: The Minerva Beamline at the ALBA synchrotron is a dedicated metrology facility operating at the soft X-ray energy range (1 keV) used to support the development, testing, and fabrication of the optics for the upcoming NewAthena X-ray space observatory, an European Space Agency (ESA) L-class mission, planned to be adopted in 2027. The building block units of the telelescope optics are the mirror modules (MM), based on the Sillicon Pore Optics (SPO) technology, initially developed by cosine company in cooperation with ESA. In this work we will provide an overview of the beamline elements and the calibration performed in the beamline required for the characterization of the MMs. Recent results on the beamline performance in terms of repeatability and stability in the characterization of the MM will be discussed.

Items.Authors: Annika Behrens, Valentin Emberger, Robert Andritschke, Günter Hauser, Astrid Mayr, Johannes Müller-Seidlitz, Léonie Sommer, Elif Kutdemir Öncü, Peter Lechner, Christian Sandow
Items.Title: Characterisation of the NewAthena WFI DEPFET detectors’ on-chip optical blocking filter
Items.Abstract: The Wide Field Imager (WFI) will be one of two instruments on the NewAthena X-ray observatory. Using Depleted P-channel Field Effect Transistor (DEPFET) sensors, it will provide imaging spectroscopy with a large field of view of 40’ x 40’ and near fano-limited energy resolution over a broad energy band from 0.2 keV to 15 keV. The DEPFET sensors are however also sensitive to optical and UV light, which necessitates the use of an optical blocking filter (OBF). WFI will employ both an external filter and an on-chip filter consisting of 90 nm of aluminium deposited directly on the DEPFET sensors. We have investigated the homogeneity and the attenuation of the on-chip OBF at varying wavelengths from UV to infrared.

Items.Authors: Léonie Sommer, Johannes Müller-Seidlitz, Valentin Emberger, Robert Andritschke, Astrid Mayr, Annika Behrens, Günter Hauser, Peter Lechner, Christian Sandow, Anna Schweingruber, Jonas Reiffers, Elif Kutdemir Öncü
Items.Title: Characterisation of the NewAthena WFI's DEPFET flight production's operational parameters
Items.Abstract: NewAthena’s Wide Field Imager (WFI) uses detectors made up from Depleted P-Channel Field Effect Transistor (DEPFET) pixels operated in rolling shutter mode. The Large Detector Array (LDA) contains a 2 × 2 array of 512 × 512 pixels Large Detectors (LDs) allowing for a field of view of 40’ × 40’ with a frame time of 2 ms while the 64 × 64 pixels Fast Detector (FD) can observe very bright X-ray sources due to a faster frame time of 80 µs. Prototype sensors (64 × 64 pixels) were used to analyse the sensor's operational range and to optimise the ASIC and DEPFET parameters i.e. current and voltage settings, as well as the DEPFET read-out timing parameters, resulting in an improved energy resolution, reduced noise and otherwise improved sensor characteristics.

Items.Authors: Remon van Gaalen, Maria Bergomi, Kalyan Kumar Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, Gabriele Umbriaco, Luca Marafatto, Silvio di Rosa, Marco Dima, Daniele Vassallo, Davide Greggio, Tânia Sofia Gomes Machado, Carmelo Arcidiacono, Roberto Ragazzoni, Tom Herbst
Items.Title: Characterising a novel 8k sCMOS detector for on-sky operations with LBT's new speckle imager
Items.Abstract: For the new speckle imager for the Large Binocular Telescope, NirvanaVIS, a novel detector has been selected, the Teledyne COSMOS-8k.  Detector performance has a large influence on the performance of the speckle holography deconvolution method envisioned for this instrument. Which benefits from a detector that has a large array of pixels, with a fast readout that can operate in a global shutter mode, like the selected COSMOS-8k.  As NirvanaVIS will utilise the on-sky proven GLAO correction provided by the LINC-NIRVANA instrument, it will have a fast track to on-sky operations and is expected to be installed at the telescope in 2027. Given that this is one of the first COSMOS-8k cameras to operate on-sky, additional interest goes out to its characterisation.  Here the procedures, processing, and results of the tests performed at the laboratories of INAF-Padova are presented.

Items.Authors: Federico Fiorentino, Ugo Lo Cicero, Luisa Sciortino, Michela Todaro, Edoardo Alaimo, Fabio D'Anca, Alberto Gulizzi, Salvatore Varisco, Claudio Saitta, Marco Barbera
Items.Title: Characterization of pinholes on polyimide-based filters for NewAthena
Items.Abstract: ESA’s large mission NewAthena will employ innovative microcalorimeter detectors to observe the universe in the soft X-Ray with unprecedented energy resolution. To protect the detectors and ensure optimal performance, it will make use of optical blocking filters consisting of a structural layer, for which the current baseline is thin polyimide films, coated with a thin aluminum layer. In this work, we present the study and characterization of pinholes in filters consisting of a thin (30 nm or 70 nm) Al layer on top of polyimide layers of various thickness (45 to 150 nm). Optical microscopy in correlation with IR spectroscopy is used to estimate the pinhole distributions and sizes, and the impact on the filter performance.

Items.Authors: Xavier Haubois, Rob van Holstein, Samuel Bonilla, Pierre Bourget, Daphnée Bregeault, Nicolas Schuhler
Items.Title: Characterization of the instrumental polarization of VLTI/ATs
Items.Abstract: The Very Large Telescope Interferometer (VLTI) provides unique capabilities for high-angular-resolution observations at milliarcsecond scales.  Combined with polarimetric capabilities of sufficient accuracy, great enhancement is to be expected in the study the study of circumstellar environments and young stellar objects, to name a few. With this talk, we present a characterization of polarization properties obtained with the ATs.  This work addresses the description of the polarimetric measurements, the estimation of the instrumental polarization arising from ATs and beam train optics, and propsect for extracting astrophysically polarized signals. This characterization provides the foundation for exploiting VLTI/AT's polarimetric capabilities for science applications and identifies paths for future improvements to the facility's polarimetric calibration.

Items.Authors: Giacomo Gorla, Claudio Macculi, Matteo D'Andrea, Guido Torrioli, Luigi Piro, Mikko Kiviranta, Achini Rathnathilaka
Items.Title: Characterization of the SQUIDs for the NewAthena X-IFU cryogenic anti-coincidence detector
Items.Abstract: This poster presents the full characterization of the new FAB 4 SQUID amplifiers developed for the CryoAC detector of the Athena X-IFU mission. The study includes voltage–flux (V–Φ) measurements, evaluation of noise performance, gain, and thermal dissipation, as well as a direct comparison with the previous FAB 3 SQUID generation. A detailed analysis of the V–Φ response as a function of the input coil current is reported, highlighting the impact of the detector operating point on the readout chain’s noise behavior. Finally, we present the first-light results of the latest CryoAC Demonstration Model 1.2, operating at 50 mK and equipped with these new SQUID devices.

Items.Authors: S. Vješnica, P. Roje, P. Kušter, M. Kretlow, M. M. Roth
Items.Title: Characterizing the Hamamatsu ORCA-Quest 2 CMOS camera for astronomical applications using laboratory measurements and on-sky time-series observations
Items.Abstract: We report a combined laboratory and on-sky characterization of the Hamamatsu ORCA-Quest 2 scientific CMOS  camera, a device widely used in quantum optics experiments but not yet commonly used for astronomical applications.  Laboratory measurements at the Deutsches Zentrum für Astrophysik using a calibrated photometric  testbench provided conversion gain, readout noise, full-well capacity, dark current, and preliminary absolute  quantum efficiency measurements, all in good agreement with the manufacturer’s specifications. On-sky time  series observations with the 1.23 m telescope at Calar Alto Observatory in Spain were used to evaluate the  photometric precision of the camera over a wide range of magnitudes by examining the scatter of differential  photometry residuals. Together, these results quantify the detector’s noise behavior and photometric performance,  enabling an assessment of its suitability for precision optical astronomy.

Items.Authors: Markus Kasper, Laura Schreiber, Emiliano Diolaiti, Silvano Desidera, Oscar Carrión-González, Siddharth Maharana, Arthur Vigan, Gaël Chauvin, Axel Potier, Matthias Tecza, Eric Stadler, Sebastiaan Haffert, Maud Langlois, Silvia Scheithauer, Carlos Correia, Stefan Ströbele, Benjamin Charnay, Emilio Carlo Molinari
Items.Title: Closing the technology gap for the Extremely Large Telescope’s planetary camera and spectrograph (ELT-PCS): description of the roadmap activity
Items.Abstract: PCS is the ELT’s planet imaging camera and spectrograph, designed for direct observation and characterization of exoplanets down to Earth-mass in the habitable zones of M-stars. The PCS R&D roadmap project is a community effort and sets out a strategic plan to define scientific requirements, instrument concept, and to analyze the capabilities and key budgets of the system, such as mass, volume, and throughput. A major goal is identifying critical enabling technologies and advancing their readiness to mitigate risks.  The roadmap also fosters collaborative training for early-career researchers in high-contrast imaging. The project structure consists of seven interdependent work packages: Science Case and Technology Readiness, Coronagraphy and Wavefront Control, Science Instruments, XAO, XAO-DM, Systems Engineering, and Science Yield Analysis. Each is jointly led by community experts. The planned deliverables include a summary white paper to support ELT PCS Phase A approval.

Items.Authors: Hervé Geoffray, Clementine Durnez, Alexandre Le Roch, Cédric Virmontois
Items.Title: CNES recent development for infrared scientific detectors: status and way forward
Items.Abstract: Growing interest for space missions with IR detection requires the constant improvement of IR detectors technologies. CNES is involved in detector developments for science missions. Design and technology enhancement are key drivers to simplify detection chain architecture. The main detector performance drivers for future missions are: linearity at low flux, low noise, medium to high frequency readout, moderate power consumption, digital output, and large format… CNES (Centre National d’Etudes Spatiales) is continuously pushing the developments to increase the maturity level of the technologies and enhance the key performances in the field of IR detections for Scientific Space missions. In this paper, we present both a status on mission with IR capabilities, for which CNES is strongly involved and CNES future developments and R&T programs.

Items.Authors: Sara Svendsen, Diego Paredes-Sanz, Sonny Massahi, Desirée Ferreira, Arne S. Jegers, Finn Christensen, Aniket Thete, Christian Körnig, David Girou, Max Collon, Dieter Skroblin, Levent Cibik, Robert Fechner, Christian Gollwitzer, Michael Krumrey, Marcos Bavdaz
Items.Title: Coating development for the NewAthena x-ray optics
Items.Abstract: The development of X-ray reflective mirror coatings for the NewAthena optics is progressing, with efforts aimed  at achieving the required effective area performance, and ensuring full compatibility with the Silicon Pore Optics  manufacturing processes.  Platinum and carbon coating designs have been demonstrated to be suitable for NewAthena, but several aspects  of thin film quality and stability must still be addressed. Particularly important is the experimental validation  of multilayer coatings, as they are an enabling technology necessary to achieve the effective area requirement for  the high-energy science cases.  We present results of coating development and characterisation of representative thin film coatings using X-ray  reflectometry.

Items.Authors: Marshall C. Johnson, Marcelo Tala Pinto, Jonathan Crass, Brian Sands, Jackson Datkuliak, Julia Brady, Michael Engelman, Daniel Pappalardo, Mark Derwent, Xavier Lesley, Justin R. Crepp, Andrew Bechter, Eric Bechter, Christian Schwab, David Aikens, Chad Bender, Chris Brandon, Cynthia Brooks, Matheus J. Castro, Jeffrey Chilcote, Al Conrad, Gregory Delo, Erin Duell, Matthew Engstrom, Steve Ertel, Sai Vidyud Senthil Nathan, Louis Fantano, John Keith Feggans, Hali Flores, Scott Gaudi, David King, Ondrej Kitzler, Kaitlin Kratter, Jeffrey Kruk, Thomas Legero, Stanimir Letchev, Jerry Mason, Joaquin Mason, Matthew Misch, Jacob Pember, Richard Pogge, Andreas Quirrenbach, Allie Renshaw, Austin Richie, Alexa Rizika, Nandini Sadagopan, Joshua Schlieder, Joseph Shields, Jonathan Shover, Mark Smithwright, James Smous, Jayde Spiegel, Julian Stürmer, Sahil Sura, Robert Switzer, Joe Thomes, Augustyn Waczynski, Ji Wang, Lauren Weiss, Daniel Wilson, Dane Zielinski-Nicolson
Items.Title: Commissioning and on-sky performance verification of iLocater
Items.Abstract: iLocater is a high-resolution near-infrared extreme precision radial velocity (EPRV) spectrograph which is being deployed to the Large Binocular Telescope (LBT) in early 2026. We present the reintegration, commissioning and initial on-sky verification program, including from both a solar feed and night-time observations with the LBT.

Items.Authors: Mackenzie R. Lach, Steph Sallum, Andrew Skemer
Items.Title: Commissioning results for the SCALES non-redundant aperture masking mode
Items.Abstract: SCALES stands for “Slicer Combined with Array of Lenslets for Exoplanet Spectroscopy” and is an integral field spectrograph (IFS) at W. M. Keck Observatory that will directly image and spectroscopically characterize circumstellar disks and young exoplanets from 2-5μm, among other scientific targets. SCALES’s low spectral resolution and imaging modes are equipped with a set of complimentary non-redundant aperture masks (NRM), which transform the telescope aperture into an interferometer and allow for improved angular resolution beyond lambda/d at moderate contrasts. We present the first commissioning results from the SCALES NRM mode. We observe several known targets, including bright stars, binaries, and stars with known protoplanetary disks in order to validate the performance of this mode. We compare our observations with prior SCALES simulations.

Items.Authors: J. C. Mason, I. Schofield, D. F. Buscher, S. Calzadilla, M. J. Creech-Eakman, E. K. R. Floyd, C. A. Haniff, J. J. D. Luis, A. Olivares, C. Salcido, E. B. Seneta, S. Rochelle, J. S. Young
Items.Title: Commissioning the infrared coherencing nearest neighbor (ICoNN) fringe tracker
Items.Abstract: The Magdalena Ridge Observatory Interferometer (MROI) has recently obtained first fringes using our first science combiner, FOURIER. As subsequent observations obtain fringes on fainter targets, the MROI will soon need a dedicated fringe tracker. The Infrared Coherencing Nearest Neighbor (ICoNN) fringe tracker is the inaugural fringe tracker for the MROI. With the MROI collecting science fringes regularly, and a third telescope scheduled to arrive in about 18 months, ICoNN has become a high priority for the observatory. ICoNN is a fringe tracker which consists of four subsystems: the switchyard, the beam combiner, the periscope optics, and the spectrograph/dewar. ICoNN operates in the H or Ks bands, to complement the scientific observations with FOURIER and maintain maximal throughput. This paper details the commissioning of ICoNN as it is upgraded to a new detector and all subsystems are integrated, tested, and deployed on sky.

Items.Authors: Jiao Ding, Yu Zhou, Ryota Hayakawa, Kaori Hattori, Tommaso Ghigna, Aritoki Suzuki, Maurice Garcia-Sciveres
Items.Title: Comprehensive microstructural and superconducting characterization of AlMn transition-edge sensors: effects of annealing, baking, and proximity to Nb leads
Items.Abstract: Superconducting Transition-Edge Sensors (TESs) using AlMn films are promising for high-resolution cryogenic detectors in future astronomy missions due to their tunable critical temperature (Tc). This study systematically examines how thermal processing—specifically annealing temperature and baking conditions—affects Tc, interface roughness, and microscopic film properties. Using current–voltage characteristics, critical current–temperature relations, and microstructural measurements, we establish direct links between processing parameters, surface morphology, and superconducting behavior. We also quantify proximity effects from Nb leads and their influence on the AlMn transition. Our results show that thermal treatments not only tune Tc but also drive significant microstructural changes that impact device performance. These findings provide guidance for optimizing fabrication protocols for high-performance AlMn TES arrays in next-generation astronomical instruments.

Items.Authors: Flavia Calderone, Isabella Pagano, Simonetta Chinellato, Valentina Viotto, Demetrio Magrin, Jacopo Farinato, Matteo Munari, Francesco Borsa, Roberto Ragazzoni, Daniele Brienza, Raffaele Piazzolla, Mario Salatti, Elisabetta Tommasi, Duncan Goulty, Joseph Huesler, Virginie Cessa, Alexis Brandeker, Emanuele Capuano, Emanuele Alberto Macrì, Giammarco Roini, Marco Nebiolo, Donata Valletti
Items.Title: Configuration management activities for the PLATO telescope optical units
Items.Abstract: ESA’s PLATO (PLAnetary Transits and Oscillations of stars) M3-class mission is designed to detect and characterise  exoplanets orbiting the habitable zone of solar-type stars through high-precision photometric observations. Its payload  contains an array of 26 Telescope Optical Units (TOUs), each one part of a multi-camera system optimised for high  photometric stability and wide-field sky coverage. During the TOUs development and production phase, which has  involved contributions from multiple institutes and industrial partners, Configuration Management (CM) has contributed  to design integrity, traceability and consistency between manufactured items and documentation throughout the design, development, AIT/AIV and lifecycle phases of the units. The main CM activities applicable to space products  and their application to the PLATO TOUs, performed by INAF in compliance with the ECSS standards, are here  outlined with a specific focus on the Document Configuration and Data Management.

Items.Authors: Pierre Vermot, Damien Gratadour, Paul Fontanillas
Items.Title: Convolutional neural networks for pyramid wavefront sensing
Items.Abstract: Pyramid wavefront sensors provide high photon efficiency but introduce nonlinearities that make standard linear reconstruction suboptimal. This work compares two supervised CNN-based reconstructors for SAXO+ pyramid-WFS residual phase control: a U-Net predicting DM actuator commands and a CNN encoder predicting modal commands. Both are trained from push–pull calibration data and benchmarked against a modal-gain-optimized linear reconstructor in three COMPASS SAXO+ reference cases. Both CNNs improve the mean 4–6 λ/D coronagraphic contrast in all cases, with the best architecture depending on observing conditions. These results support nonlinear CNN reconstruction as a practical route to improved pyramid-WFS control.

Items.Authors: Kohji Tsumura, Hideo Matsuhara, Koji Kawabata, Hiroshi Akitaya, Shuji Matsuura, Rinon Kageyama, Tomoya Hori, Haruaki Niinuma, Keisuke Shinozaki, Ryo Hashimoto, Hiroshi Tomida, Akihiro Doi, Daisuke Yonetoku
Items.Title: Cryogenic optical test plan for the visible and near-infrared telescope MONSTER onboard HiZ-GUNDAM satellite
Items.Abstract: The HiZ-GUNDAM mission is dedicated to time-domain and multi-messenger astronomy focusing on gamma-ray bursts (GRBs). It is designed to deliver rapid alerts of high-redshift GRBs with photometric redshift provided by MONSTER, a 30-cm visible and near-infrared telescope onboard the satellite. After launch at ambient temperature, MONSTER is cooled to <200 K and its near-infrared detector to <120 K via radiative cooling, enabling high sensitivity in the near-infrared. The telescope employs an athermal design using a single aluminum alloy, ensuring uniform thermal contraction and stable image performance across temperatures. To validate this concept, a breadboard model (BBM) of MONSTER has been built for cryogenic optical testing. Beginning in April 2026, we plan to cool the BBM to operational temperature and conduct optical performance evaluations. This presentation summarizes the current development status of MONSTER, with emphasis on preparations for the BBM cryogenic optical tests.

Items.Authors: Yuan Li, Yasuhiro Hirahara, Ryoichi Koga, Umi Enokidani, Shunsuke Baba, Hideo Matsuhara, Takao Nakagawa, Takehiko Wada
Items.Title: Cryogenic transmittance measurements of large high-resistivity CdZnTe for immersion grating applications in the GREX-PLUS mid-infrared high-resolution spectrometer
Items.Abstract: We are developing a high-resolution mid-infrared spectrograph (HRS) with a cadmium zinc telluride (CdZnTe) immersion grating (IG) for the GREX-PLUS mission. The HRS aims to achieve a resolving power of R∼30,000 over 10–18 µm, requiring a high-index material with sufficiently low absorption at cryogenic temperatures. In our previous work, we demonstrated that high-resistivity CdZnTe (∼10^10 Ωcm) satisfies this requirement at ≤20 K. Building on this result, large (∼6 inch) CdZnTe ingots have recently been fabricated, enabling extraction of IG-sized blanks. We report new transmission measurements of 1 and 10 mm-thick samples cut near the extraction region of a large ingot with the same crystallographic orientation as the IG optical axis. The samples show a resistivity of ∼10^9 Ωcm. We also improved thermal stabilization of the measurement system and investigated the rapid increase in transmittance below ∼10 K, possibly due to freeze out of residual electrons.

Items.Authors: Pierpaolo Merola, Mauro Focardi
Items.Title: Cryo-harness shielding effectiveness assessment for ARIEL mission of the ESA’s Cosmic Vision Program
Items.Abstract: A simulation campaign has been carried out to assess the shielding effectiveness for the ARIEL mission. The analysis focuses particularly on the most sensitive cryo-cables, located outside the payload and the service module cavity. For all the instrument cable sets, conducted and radiated susceptibility analyses have been performed, including the evaluation of the transfer impedance (Zₜ). Time-domain analyses are also included to test the harness impulsive susceptibility and its response to transients. Special attention is given to the number of bonding connections and the maximum allowable resistance to the spacecraft reference ground. The simulation campaign has been performed using numerical electromagnetic analysis tools based on the Finite Element Method and Transmission Line Theory. The outcome of this study will be used to define appropriate reference requirements for the payload, ensuring that the harness design meets the necessary EM compatibility and performance.
